Conceptual Study Guide — Units 1 to 5
Written in simple language, with a diagram in each unit and a memory hook for every idea.
How to Use This Guide
Every unit follows the same shape: WHAT it is → HOW it works → WHY it matters → MNEMONIC → QUICK TEST.
The mnemonics are the 'cheat codes' — you can recall the whole unit from the short phrase alone.
Do the Quick Test at the end of each unit. Answers are one line below the question.
Look at the diagram at the end of each unit — it makes the text click.
UNIT 1 — BACTERIA (Prokaryotic Cell)
What Is It?

Bacteria are the oldest, simplest, and most numerous living things on Earth. A single drop of soil water can hold millions of them. They are prokaryotes — tiny cells that do NOT have a real nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Their DNA just floats free in the cell, called the nucleoid.
Why It Matters
Some bacteria are harmful (they cause disease).
But most are helpful: they make your food (yogurt, curd, cheese, bread rise), fix nitrogen in the soil for plants, and break down waste so the planet stays clean.
Because a bacterium is a single cell, 'cell' and 'organism' are the same thing.
How It Is Built — 6 Must-Know Parts
Cell wall (peptidoglycan) — A stiff jacket that keeps shape and stops bursting.
Cell membrane (plasma membrane) — The gate that decides what goes in and out.
Cytoplasm — The jelly filling.
Nucleoid / DNA loop — The genetic instructions, with NO nuclear membrane. This is the #1 exam fact: 'no true nucleus'.
Ribosomes (70S) — Little protein-building machines, but smaller than eukaryote ones.

Optional extras — Flagellum (tail for swimming), pili (hairy threads to grab surfaces / swap DNA), plasmid (small extra DNA ring, often carries antibiotic-resistance genes), capsule (slime coat for protection).
Mnemonic
'WALL · MEMBRANE · JELLY · GOLD · RIE'
WALL → Cell wall
MEMBRANE → Cell membrane
JELLY → Cytoplasm (the jelly inside)
GOLD → DNA / Nucleoid (the 'gold standard' instruction book, no nucleus)
RIE → Ribosomes + the extras (flagellum, pili, plasmid)
Shorter hook: a Prokaryote's life is 'No Nucleus, No Organelles, just ONE DNA ring + wall + membrane.' → 'No-No-One' = prokaryote.
Quick Test
Q1. Do bacteria have a nucleus? → No; their DNA is a naked loop (nucleoid).
Q2. What makes the cell wall stiff? → Peptidoglycan.
Q3. Which part lets a bacterium swim? → Flagellum (the tail).
Q4. What is a plasmid? → A small separate loop of DNA that often carries 'extra' genes, like antibiotic resistance.
